name: Fetaui Khoury-Lautoa
role: Underground press operator and anti-corporate journalist
location: Highland Park Autonomous Zone, near Lake Shore Drive and North
description:
Nneka is compact and relentless, with deep brown skin mapped by a constellation of small data-port scars she refuses to have removed — each one a story she got burned getting. Her hair cycles through slow bioluminescent pulses of indigo and amber, a mod she got at nineteen and has never upgraded because she likes the old-fashioned glow. She wears ink-stained fingerless gloves almost constantly and has the slightly haunted look of someone who hasn't slept a full night in years.

She runs 'Fault Lines,' a zine-and-broadcast hybrid that drops every ten days via pirated Ferrogate Transit screens, cheap paper drops in laundromat stalls, and encrypted mesh nodes. Her reporting has cost two mid-tier Axiom managers their contracts, exposed a Tessera water-rationing fraud scheme, and made her a minor legend in the Autonomous Zone. She is funny in person — quicker to a laugh than her reputation suggests — but she does not forgive sources who lie to her twice, and she does not apologize for stories that are true.

core_fears: Losing the trust of the community she covers
core_desires: Accountability — for it to mean something, not just print
To be known as honest rather than brave
coping_mechanisms: Throws herself into the next story when the last one didn't change anything
Keeps meticulous source logs as a way of feeling in control
blind_spots: Assumes her editorial instincts are neutral when they have clear ideological lean
Underestimates how much her platform depends on a handful of key relationships
psychology.secret: She buried a story two years ago because the subject was a mutual aid coordinator she personally loved. The woman was embezzling. Nneka has never published a word about it and has never fully admitted to herself that she made an editorial decision out of loyalty.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Punchy, declarative, minimal jargon — she writes like she talks and talks like she's always filing copy
speech_patterns.cadence: Fast when passionate, deliberately slow when she wants something to land
verbal_tics: 'That's the version or that's what happened?'
example_lines: Put it on record — Tessera doesn't ration water because the grid can't handle it. They ration it because scarcity is a product.
I don't do anonymous unless I can verify three ways. Those are my terms. You don't like the terms, you find another press.

story_hooks: She's sitting on a source document that implicates someone in the players' orbit and is waiting for a second confirmation she can't get on her own
Fault Lines' print infrastructure is being systematically sabotaged — someone is destroying her distribution nodes one by one and she needs to figure out who before the next issue drops
narrative_function: Information broker and local legend — players can trade scoops for access to her network, and she can surface rumors, expose backstory, or drag a situation into public light at a critical moment.
augmentations: Three legacy data-port scars (non-functional, cosmetic remnant of old hardware). Bioluminescent hair mod. Subdermal quick-copy chip in her left palm that stores up to 40 hours of audio.
daily_life: Wakes before dawn to check encrypted drops from sources, spends mornings writing and editing in her print shop apartment, afternoons doing interviews or attending council meetings, evenings laying out the next issue or broadcasting from a rotating set of rooftop nodes.
affiliation: Fault Lines Independent Press; loose network of community councils across the Autonomous Zone

decision_rules: Verify before publishing, no exceptions — one retraction poisons a hundred truths
Never burn a source who played straight with her
escalation_ladder: Polite professional distance with new contacts
Direct questioning if she senses evasion
Cold, precise confrontation if she has documentation contradicting what she's being told

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Professionally warm but evaluating — everyone is a potential source or a potential liability
interpersonal_modes.friends: Generous, irreverent, fiercely loyal within her own strict moral code

stress_responses.low: Makes dark jokes about the news cycle
stress_responses.medium: Goes quiet and productive — disappears into research
stress_responses.high: Publishes something — even if it's not ready, she needs the act of release

contradictions: Believes in transparency absolutely but guards her own emotional life like classified files
habits: Reads every issue of Fault Lines aloud before it goes out — 'if I can't say it, it's not ready'
Leaves small data offerings at the E.L.F. shrine in her building's server room before major drops
breaking_points: Discovering a source has been a corporate plant the entire time
Being ordered by a community council to kill a story for political reasons

related_entities: Zheng-Dao Heavy Industries Containment Foam Launcher CFL-2 'Amber'

physical_description.heritage: Pacific Islander (Polynesian/Melanesian base) with Middle Eastern, Eastern European, Hispanic, and Sub-Saharan African ancestry creating a warm, complex phenotype. Dominant Pacific Islander features with subtle blending from secondary ancestries.
physical_description.build: Compact and wiry, lean muscle from years of climbing rooftops and moving through tight urban spaces. No excess weight; chest slightly narrow, shoulders squared. Moves like someone used to fitting into spaces others can't reach.
physical_description.hair_color: Natural black base with slow bioluminescent pulse cycling indigo-to-amber
physical_description.hair_style: Worn loose and shoulder-length, often pulled back with a strip of repurposed copper wire or fabric scraps. Occasionally braided when working in the print shop to keep the glow from obscuring her eyes.
physical_description.eye_color: Deep brown, alert and slightly red-rimmed from chronic sleep deprivation
physical_description.skin_tone: Warm medium-to-deep brown with golden and amber undertones, reflecting strong Pacific Islander ancestry blended with subtle warmth from Middle Eastern and Sub-Saharan heritage
physical_description.complexion: High cheekbones with rounded fullness characteristic of Pacific Islander features, angular jaw refined by Eastern European ancestry. Skin texture shows fatigue — slight hollowness under the eyes, faint laugh lines around her mouth from sardonic humor. No makeup; a faint chemical burn scar traces her left temple from a printing-press accident at twenty-four. Overall complexion warm and sun-kissed despite urban life.
distinguishing_marks: Three small circular data-port scars arranged vertically along the inner left forearm, each about the size of a pill capsule, left deliberately unhealed as visible testimony to old hardware she refuses to erase.
Chemical burn scar on left temple — thin and pale, running from hairline toward her cheekbone, slightly raised and shiny with age.
Ink stains on the webbing between her thumb and index finger on both hands (permanent, from years of press work), darker on her left hand where she favors it for writing.
Small tattoo on her inner right wrist — a stylized ferrogate symbol with the date '2214' below it (marks the day Axiom tried to shut down the first Fault Lines broadcast).
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Bioluminescent hair that pulses with slow indigo-to-amber color cycles (old tech, visible from across a room in dim light). Three data-port scars on left forearm. Subdermal quick-copy chip in left palm is not visibly obvious but creates a slight luminous line under the skin when active (rarely shows). Ink stains and wear patterns on her fingerless gloves suggest constant data-work.
physical_description.posture_movement: Moves with economical precision — no wasted motion. Shoulders slightly forward from hunching over design work. Head tilts when listening, as if calibrating. Hands move expressively when speaking but settle into stillness when thinking. Habitual thumb-drum on whatever surface is nearest when anxious. Walks fast, always looks like she's going somewhere specific even when she's not.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 3-4 working class with intentional anti-corporate edge. Favors dark, durable fabrics (cotton-poly blends, canvas). Fingerless work gloves in faded charcoal, worn constantly. Oversized button-up shirt (often men's cut, often with sleeves rolled) layered over fitted tank tops in black or dark gray. Cargo pants or heavy denim with multiple pockets for micro-recorders and data chips. Scuffed steel-toed boots (practical for rooftop work). A battered vinyl jacket from a vintage thrift-market, patched with fabric remnants from old Fault Lines print runs. Often wears a repurposed Tessera ID badge on a cord around her neck (non-functional, kept as a trophy from the water-rationing expose). No jewelry except a slim bracelet woven from copper wire and colored thread — handmade, looks fragile but isn't.
